# Blueprint

> From one recurring task to a measured robot pilot. Blueprint runs a free beta: a site shows one recurring task, invited robot teams evaluate it in simulation, and Blueprint recommends one team whose evaluation on that job passed.

Blueprint runs a free beta for real sites and recurring tasks. Sign-up is open for sites: anyone can start a job by describing it or sharing permitted video, and Blueprint also onboards sites by hand. Invited robot teams evaluate the site's job free, in a simplified simulation of the task, informed by the site's footage. Blueprint recommends one team whose evaluation on that job passed and that wants the pilot; the site books it in one step and never has to compare teams. During the beta nothing is charged to sites or robot teams: no site fee, no paid private evaluations, balances, top-ups or checkout. After booking, the site and the robot team agree the physical pilot's dates and terms directly, and Blueprint takes no cut. Simulation results are bounded estimates: simulation is not physical proof or a deployment guarantee, and it never certifies physical performance or safety.

- [Privacy](https://tryblueprint.io/privacy)
- [Terms](https://tryblueprint.io/terms)

Robot teams register interest through the existing application and join by invitation. Applications remain pending until manual approval for a real site task; applying or creating an account does not grant access. Approved teams see only job cards sites chose to share, and evaluate invited jobs free. A task invitation does not guarantee a run, a recommendation, or a deployment. Paid self-service evaluations and top-ups are disabled during the beta. Beta program: https://tryblueprint.io/beta. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

Customer wording uses “job” for the work a site wants automated and “task” for the specific robot action and its technical conditions. API fields and identifiers retain their existing names.

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.

## Agent interfaces and compatibility

Current public/request tools are `blueprint.siteWorld.search`, `blueprint.catalog.search`, `blueprint.ask`, `blueprint.request.locationDraft`, `blueprint.siteWorld.get`, and `blueprint.siteWorld.launchReadiness`.

The historical read and hosted-session compatibility tools are `blueprint.commerce.order.get`, `blueprint.commerce.liveOrder.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlement.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlementReadiness`, `blueprint.session.create`, `blueprint.session.reset`, `blueprint.session.step`, `blueprint.session.runBatch`, `blueprint.session.control`, `blueprint.session.renderExplorer`, and `blueprint.session.export`. Historical availability does not make these current standalone products.

Team tools are `blueprint.team.me`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.register`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.list`, `blueprint.team.plan`, `blueprint.team.runs.start`, `blueprint.team.runs.release`, `blueprint.team.policy.get`, and `blueprint.team.policy.set`. Team account and checkpoint tools use a revocable per-team agent key bound to a verified Blueprint account. Early-access library admission remains required (403 `early_access_required` otherwise). During the free beta, paid planning, dry-run purchase, run-start and top-up APIs return 403 `paid_evaluations_disabled`, including requests with `confirm: true`. Request an invited evaluation through the workspace. Execution requires operator approval of the exact team, policy, task, current rights, expiry, one attempt, and a separate Blueprint-funded compute limit. Historical balances and receipts remain available under their original access controls.

Truth labels are `capture_grounded`, `provider_derived`, `generated`, `request_gated`, `protected_robot_team`, `legacy_commerce_read_only`, and `decision_or_abstention`.
